questions.question: What is anaerobic exercise?
questions.solution_html:
• Anaerobic exercise is a type of high-intensity physical activity where the body's demand for
  • oxygen exceeds the oxygen supply available, so the body relies on energy sources stored in the muscles
  • rather than oxygen from breathing. Examples include: – Sprinting– Weightlifting– High-intensity interval
  • training (HIIT)– Jumping or plyometrics. It is mainly used to build strength, power, and muscle mass, and
  • to improve short bursts of speed.

questions.question: Define flexibility. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Define flexibility.
  • • Flexibility is the ability of a joint or muscle to move through its full range of motion.
  • • It depends on the elasticity of muscles and ligaments.

questions.question: What is the definition of health according to the World Health Organization?
questions.solution_html:
• According to the World Health Organization (WHO), health is defined as: "A state of complete
  • physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity."

questions.question: What is meant by diet quality? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is meant by diet quality?
  • • Diet quality means how healthy and balanced the food intake is.
  • • It depends on nutrients, variety, and moderation in food choices.

questions.question: What is adaptation in the context of physical training?
questions.solution_html:
• Adaptation in the context of physical training refers to the body’s physiological response to
  • repeated exercise, where it gradually becomes more efficient and better able to handle physical stress.
  • For example:– Muscles become stronger– Endurance improves– The cardiovascular system works more
  • efficiently. This process allows an individual to perform exercises with greater ease or at higher
  • intensities over time.

questions.question: Explain lifestyle diseases. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain lifestyle diseases.
  • • Lifestyle diseases are illnesses caused by unhealthy habits and poor daily routines.
  • • Examples include obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and heart disease.

questions.question: What is the circadian rhythm?
questions.solution_html:
• Circadian rhythm is the natural, internal process that regulates the sleep-wake cycle and repeats
  • roughly every 24 hours. It influences various bodily functions such as:– Sleep patterns– Hormone
  • release– Body temperature– Digestion. The circadian rhythm is mainly controlled by the brain's
  • hypothalamus, and it is affected by external cues like light and darkness.

questions.question: What are flat feet, and how do they develop? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What are flat feet, and how do they develop?
  • • Flat feet are a condition in which the arches of the feet are low or absent.
  • • They may develop due to weak muscles, poor posture, obesity, injury, or heredity.

questions.question: What is correct posture, and why is it important?
questions.solution_html:
• Correct posture refers to the alignment of the body in such a way that the bones, muscles, and
  • joints are positioned to avoid unnecessary strain. In a standing position, this means:– The head is aligned
  • with the spine. – Shoulders are relaxed and level. – The back is straight with a natural curve in the lower
  • back. – Knees are slightly bent, and weight is evenly distributed across both feet.
  • Importance of Correct Posture: Prevents musculoskeletal issues, improves breathing and digestion,
  • Boosts energy levels, Enhances confidence.

questions.question: What is a strain? / [CO2] [5x2 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• What is a strain?
  • • A strain is an injury caused by overstretching or tearing of a muscle or tendon.
  • • It usually happens due to sudden force or overuse.

questions.question: Discuss the need and importance of Physical Education in today’s fast-paced and technology-driven society / [CO1]

• Discuss the need and importance of Physical Education in today’s fast-paced and
  • technology-driven society

  • • It improves physical fitness, endurance, and motor skills.

  • • It promotes discipline, teamwork, and healthy habits.

questions.question: What is nutrition? Explain the classification of nutrients and their role in maintaining health.
questions.solution_html:
• Nutrition refers to the process by which the body takes in and uses food for growth, energy, and overall
  • health. It involves the intake of essential substances from food, which are then absorbed and utilized by
  • the body for various physiological functions.
  • Classification of Nutrients: Nutrients are substances required by the body for growth, energy, and proper
  • functioning. They are classified into macronutrients and micronutrients, each playing a crucial role in
  • maintaining health.
  • Explain its role and sources of macronutrients and micronutrients

questions.question: Explain the classification of nutrients and their role in maintaining overall health. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the classification of nutrients and their role in maintaining overall
  • health.
  • • Nutrients are classified as carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water, and
  • roughage.
  • • Carbohydrates provide energy.
  • • Proteins help growth and repair of tissues.
  • • Fats provide concentrated energy and support cell function.
  • • Vitamins and minerals regulate body processes and protect health.
  • • Water and roughage support digestion and hydration.

questions.question: What are dietary supplements? Discuss their potential benefits and risks?
questions.solution_html:
• Dietary supplements are products taken orally that contain nutrients or other substances
  • intended to supplement the diet. They can include vitamins, minerals, herbs, amino acids, enzymes, or
  • other bioactive compounds. They come in various forms such as tablets, capsules, powders, liquids, and
  • gummies.
  • Examples include: – Vitamin D tablets – Iron supplements – Protein powders – Omega-3 capsules –
  • Herbal supplements like echinacea or ginseng
  • Potential Benefits of Dietary Supplements

questions.question: What are the dangers of overusing or misusing dietary supplements? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What are the dangers of overusing or misusing dietary supplements?
  • • They may cause toxicity and side effects.
  • • They can interfere with medicines.
  • • They may create false confidence and poor diet habits.
  • • Excess intake of some vitamins and minerals may harm organs.
  • • Misuse may lead to unnecessary expense and health risks.

questions.question: Explain the procedure of the Harvard Step Test and how it measures cardiovascular fitness. / [CO3] [3x5 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the procedure of the Harvard Step Test and how it measures
  • cardiovascular fitness.
  • • The Harvard Step Test is a fitness test used to assess cardiovascular endurance.
  • • The person steps up and down on a bench at a fixed rate for a fixed time.
  • • After exercise, pulse rate is measured during recovery.
  • • A faster recovery pulse shows better cardiovascular fitness.
  • • It is simple, practical, and widely used in physical education.
